sleepers.name: Rico Dowdle
sleepers.why: Signed with PIT in free agency; through Steelers camp he has clearly won the RB1 job over Jaylen Warren, giving him a full early-down/goal-line workload his ADP was set before.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Panthers/Steelers camp reports, late Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
sleepers.why: Commanders traded away Brian Robinson Jr.; Croskey-Merritt (785 yds, 8 TD in 2025) has taken over as Washington's RB1 on the first unofficial 2026 depth chart in Kliff Kingsbury's offense, well ahead of new addition Rachaad White.
sleepers.source: CBSSports/Sportscasting Commanders depth chart, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Jonathon Brooks
sleepers.why: Camp reports have Brooks in a legitimate 1B role and possibly overtaking Chuba Hubbard atop Carolina's backfield after Rico Dowdle left for Pittsburgh removed the incumbent early-down back.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Panthers backfield report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Blake Corum
sleepers.why: Widely called the top handcuff in fantasy behind Kyren Williams, who has a real injury history (high ankle sprain in 2025). Corum's own role grew after a strong 2025 second half.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Rams handcuff report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Kenny Gainwell
sleepers.why: Left Philadelphia to sign with Tampa Bay as the direct backup/receiving-down complement to Bucky Irving, who is coming off shoulder surgery and missed 7 games in 2025 — real standalone PPR value if Irving's shoulder flares again.
sleepers.source: ProFootballNetwork/FantasyLife Bucs backfield report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: RJ Harvey
sleepers.why: Rookie clearly the presumed RB2 in Denver's committee behind J.K. Dobbins, with real touch share in a run-committed offense rather than a token role.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Broncos depth chart debate, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: J.K. Dobbins
sleepers.why: Fully healthy and named the clear Broncos starter for 2026 after an injury-shortened track record depressed his ADP; still gets first crack at lead work in a run-committed Denver offense.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Broncos RB depth chart, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Chuba Hubbard
sleepers.why: Still Carolina's proven, more complete back (receiving + goal line) even as Brooks pushes for touches; profiles as underpriced floor if he wins the competition outright.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Panthers backfield report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Jordan Mason
sleepers.why: Camp reports have Mason outplaying Aaron Jones Sr. and co-starting Minnesota's backfield after a strong training camp, with some outlets calling him the safer-floor back of the pair.
sleepers.source: Yahoo Sports/TheBigLead Vikings RB camp report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Michael Wilson
sleepers.why: Signed a 3-year, $75M extension after a 1,000-yard 2025 breakout; target share rose to 23-27% whenever Marvin Harrison Jr. was out or limited, and MHJ's injury history (appendicitis, heel/foot) is real ongoing risk that keeps funneling volume to Wilson.
sleepers.source: NFL.com/RaisingZona Cardinals WR report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Alec Pierce
sleepers.why: Projected as Indianapolis's actual WR1 with a 24-27% target share, ahead of Josh Downs, after a 1,003-yard, 21.3 YPC 2025 season — his ADP still reflects his old boom/bust deep-threat-only profile.
sleepers.source: SI.com Onsi Colts WR target-share projection, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Matthew Golden
sleepers.why: Rookie ascending fast in Green Bay's receiver room as Christian Watson battles injury history and Romeo Doubs/Dontayvion Wicks are gone; Golden projects as the clear 1a/1b target earner.
sleepers.source: RotoWire/FantasyPros Packers WR sleeper coverage, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
sleepers.why: Left NYG for a 4-year, $78M deal with Tennessee, reuniting with OC Brian Daboll; locked in as one of Cam Ward's top-3 wideouts and could become Ward's most-targeted receiver in a retooled passing offense.
sleepers.source: ProFootballNetwork/Establish The Run Titans free agency report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Jordan Addison
sleepers.why: Active with no suspension entering 2026 (unlike his 3-game ban last year), motivated in a contract year, and still benefits from Justin Jefferson drawing coverage — clean bounce-back setup after a down 2025.
sleepers.source: Heavy.com/CBSSports Vikings WR report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Jakobi Meyers
sleepers.why: Now with Jacksonville (traded from LV) alongside Brian Thomas Jr., giving him a real route-runner/possession role in a much higher-volume passing offense than his old Raiders situation.
sleepers.source: ESPN/Jaguars.com trade report
sleepers.note: trade occurred prior offseason cycle; verify current-year role before drafting

sleepers.name: Travis Hunter
sleepers.why: ESPN's model discounts him hard for splitting reps at CB, but Jacksonville has committed to increasing his offensive snaps in year 2; talent and target competition upside far exceed his ADP-implied floor.
sleepers.source: Beat-writer camp coverage, Aug 2026 (verify Week 1 offensive snap count)

sleepers.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
sleepers.why: Preseason breakout for Las Vegas — 11 catches for 109 yards on 13 targets across two preseason games — pushing his ADP up from the 13th round toward the 10th as camp progressed.
sleepers.source: FantasyPros/Roto Street Journal preseason sleeper coverage, Sept 2026

sleepers.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
sleepers.why: Rookie set to be Lamar Jackson's WR2 in Baltimore's Declan Doyle-designed offense; ADP still treats him as a camp body rather than a real Week 1 role.
sleepers.source: Roundup of Ravens camp sleeper coverage, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Khalil Shakir
sleepers.why: Buffalo's target funnel underneath in a run-heavy but efficient Josh Allen offense; steady target hog role makes him a PPR floor play priced like a WR4.
sleepers.source: General 2026 Bills WR outlook coverage

sleepers.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
sleepers.why: Fully healthy for the first time in two years and now Baker Mayfield's clear go-to target with Mike Evans gone from Tampa's WR room for the first time since 2013.
sleepers.source: JoeBucsFan/CBSSports Bucs WR health report, Aug 2026

sleepers.name: Tyler Shough
sleepers.why: Rushing floor QB2 candidate: 4.6-speed at 6'5/219, at least 6 carries in 4 straight games late in his 2025 rookie run, averaging 17.6 PPR pts/gm from Week 9 on. Included here as a bonus flex-value dart, separate from the dedicated late-QB picks below.
sleepers.source: ProFootballNetwork Tyler Shough outlook, Aug 2026

late_qb.name: Bo Nix
late_qb.why: Back-to-back QB7 finishes with a real rushing floor; adds Jaylen Waddle to a Sean Payton offense he now has two years of experience running. Best combination of proven rushing production and receiving-corps upgrade among the late-QB tier.

late_qb.name: Tyler Shough
late_qb.why: Dual-threat build (4.6 speed, 6'5/219) with legitimate weekly rushing production down the stretch of his rookie year (6+ carries in 4 straight games); projected for 4,296 pass yds / 296 rush yds / 28 total TD in year 2 as the unquestioned Saints starter.

late_te.name: Dallas Goedert
late_te.why: Remains Philadelphia's clear receiving TE1 in an offense that funnels a heavy short-to-intermediate target share his way; safest floor of the late-TE tier.

late_te.name: Jake Ferguson
late_te.why: Dallas's primary receiving TE with a full route tree role in a pass-heavy offense; target share upside if any Cowboys WR misses time.

late_te.name: Isaiah Likely
late_te.why: Signed a 3-year, $40M deal with the Giants; ESPN's Dan Graziano tabbed him a breakout-star candidate, and with Malik Nabers' Week 1 status uncertain after his ACL/meniscus surgery, Likely could open the season as New York's true #1 receiving target.
late_te.source: Heavy.com/ESPN Giants TE breakout coverage, Aug-Sept 2026
